lead.title: Elypta publishes evidence that a simple urine test flags adults at high risk of cancer within five years, across 5,436 people
lead.deck: The Solna-based Swedish medtech published a pre-registered study (NCT05235009) on the Dutch Lifelines cohort in Cancer Epidemiology, Biomarkers & Prevention: its urine score built on three glycosaminoglycans (the "GAGome"), combined with age and smoking history, places 13% to 23% of participants in a "high-risk" group that accounts for 54% of cancers diagnosed within five years, with the strongest effect in cancers that are not screened for today (pancreas, kidney, brain, lymphoma). The authors stress that independent prospective validation is still needed, but for a still-independent, ISO 13485-certified company that launched its MIRAM kit in October, this is the clinical data that opens the door to triaging populations ahead of costlier multi-cancer screening tests.

milestone.title: Molecular Designs wins its first FDA clearance for a flu A, flu B and RSV PCR panel (K262789)
milestone.summary: The physician-founded molecular test maker cleared its SimplicityDx Panel FluA/FluB/RSV, a multiplex real-time RT-PCR that detects and differentiates influenza A, influenza B and respiratory syncytial virus from anterior nasal swabs. Its breakaway format lets labs run only the tests they need, with minimal pipetting.
milestone.why: Moving from a research-use-only catalogue to a first cleared diagnostic changes the nature of a young diagnostics company: it can sell to clinical labs and build recurring consumables revenue. It is also a comparable for European respiratory-testing players facing established platforms (Cepheid, bioMérieux, Roche).

brefsEurope.title: EPFL spin-off Neurosoft Bioelectronics wins gold in biotechnology at the Fujian Global Innovation and Entrepreneurship Competition
brefsEurope.summary: The Geneva start-up, which is industrialising soft cortical electrodes (SOFT ECOG) for epilepsy and motor restoration in people with paralysis, was picked from more than 1,000 projects; it is preparing an international expansion of its clinical trials and a presence in China. A European brain-computer interface to watch, six months after its $7.5M seed.

brefsIntl.title: Natera and Incyte launch NEXERA-204, a phase II trial in which the Signatera ctDNA blood test decides who gets treated
brefsIntl.summary: The study targets stage II or III colorectal cancer patients who have had surgery and chemotherapy and whose Signatera test turns positive with no sign on imaging; they will receive INCA33890, Incyte's PD-1 × TGFβR2 bispecific antibody. The companion diagnostic becomes both an inclusion criterion and an endpoint: a template for European molecular residual disease companies.

brefsIntl.title: Accuray closes its TCW restructuring: $40M of debt converted into preferred stock
brefsIntl.summary: The maker of CyberKnife and TomoTherapy radiotherapy systems swaps a $40M term loan for convertible preferred stock, also converts July's $15M investment, gets covenant relief through end-2027 and gives TCW two board seats, after a 1-for-40 reverse stock split. A comparable on financial pressure in radiotherapy, a market where Sweden's Elekta competes.

brefsIntl.title: A rapid tuberculosis PCR test run on a simple tongue swab matches the Xpert Ultra reference in Open Forum Infectious Diseases
brefsIntl.summary: The DASH MTB test, developed by Northwestern engineers with the University of Washington and the universities of Cape Town and Stellenbosch, works on sputum or tongue swabs and returns a result within the clinic visit. Sampling the tongue, without sputum, is what matters for mass point-of-care screening.

word.fr: Screening for several cancers with one test
word.definition: A single test, usually a blood draw (sometimes urine), that looks in a person without symptoms for the biological traces left by several cancer types at once, including those for which no screening exists.

parts.label: Biomarker
parts.role: the signal measured: circulating tumour DNA (methylation, fragments), proteins or metabolites such as glycosaminoglycans

parts.label: Algorithm
parts.role: the machine-learning model that separates the "cancer" signal from noise and often predicts the organ of origin

parts.label: Confirmation pathway
parts.role: the imaging and biopsy that follow a positive test, without which the result has no clinical value

how.t: A blood or urine sample is collected from an adult without symptoms, typically aged 45 to 75.
The lab measures the biomarker profile (circulating DNA sequencing or mass spectrometry) and the algorithm computes a risk score or a positive/negative signal.
If a signal is found, the patient is referred for targeted diagnostic work-up; the challenge is to limit false positives and unnecessary procedures.

word.why: Organised screening covers only a handful of cancers (breast, colon, cervix, lung): a test targeting dozens addresses a potentially massive market, but proof of a mortality benefit does not exist yet. The US National Cancer Institute launched the Vanguard study (up to 24,000 people) to prepare a large randomised trial: for an investor, value hinges on the quality of clinical data, cost per test and the ability to target people at risk, which leaves room for alternatives to DNA such as urinary metabolites.

startups.name: Adela
